```{r setup, include=FALSE}
  "Burundi" = "BDI",

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

fmt_era_yr <- function (y) {
  paste0(as.integer(y), "AD")
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", fmt_era_yr(yrs[i_pk]), ")")
}

  "kenya_highlands_maasai_rift",
  "buganda_bunyoro_ankole",
  "rwanda_burundi_kivu",

entry_sub_ids <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
  s <- subregion_lookup[[e$key]]
  if (is.null(s)) "zanzibar_swahili_omani_coast" else s
}, character(1))

zone_entries <- setNames(lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- all_entries[entry_sub_ids == sid]
  pks <- vapply(sub, function (e) max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population))), numeric(1))
  sub[order(-pks, vapply(sub, function (e) e$name, character(1)))]
}), subregion_order)

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- iso3_map[[as.character(e$country)]]
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    data.frame(
      Settlement = as.character(e$name),
      Location = loc_str,
      `1500AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1500),
      `1700AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1700),
      `1800AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1800),
      `1850AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1850),
      `1880AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1880),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1500, 1700, 1770, 1800, 1850, 1880)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates and multi-period population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across 13 countries in East Africa and Mozambique between 1500AD and 1885AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate ports, royal capitals, *prazo* strongholds and caravan entrepôts (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` excluded as duplicate aliases), the retained ledger spans nine historical sub-regions from the Banadir and Swahili coasts through the Great Lakes and Unyamwezi to the Zambezi basin and Gaza. Active interpolated sites rise from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1500"]], 0L)` around 1500AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1700"]], 0L)` at 1700AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1800"]], 0L)` at 1800AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1850"]], 0L)` at 1850AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1880"]], 0L)` at 1880AD, documenting urban trajectories from Bigo bya Mugenyi (100k) and Muqdisho (21,2k) to Zanzibar (65k), Kibuga (38,5k), Mombasa (30k) and Tabora (20k).

# Background

Compiling an early modern settlement ledger across East Africa and Mozambique requires integrating coastal European, Arabic and Swahili sources with inland archaeological surveys and nineteenth-century travel journals [@HortonMiddleton2000Swahili; @Newitt1995Mozambique; @Burton1904FirstFootsteps]. While stone-built coral ports from Somalia to Mozambique Island and Portuguese fortresses at Sofala, Sena and Tete generated dated garrison and customs counts from the sixteenth century onward [@Pradines2016PortugueseFortresses; @Berg1900TheSwahili], earthen capitals across Buganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Unyamwezi and the Zambezi plateau relied on mapped enclosure areas and traveller headcounts recorded predominantly between 1798AD and 1885AD [@Kafuuma2019HeritageSignificance; @Bryndina2023TheMost].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Sub-Regional Partition

Candidate sites were screened across four waves from archival censuses, archaeological site inventories and historical monographs [@NMK2021KenyaSites; @Alders2023OpenAccess; @WynneJones2018SwahiliWorld]. From `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` initial entries inside the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² regional boundary clipped to geoBoundaries outlines [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate orthographies and merged aliases were excluded, leaving `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` observations. Ninety-one entries fall strictly inside the 5-arcminute regional mask pixels and 6 border-margin sites (Muqdisho, Afgoye, Baar Dheere, Chencha, Great Zimbabwe and Thulamela) are assigned to their adjoining cultural sub-regions so every entry is catalogued.

## Site-Specific Population Estimation

Every entry records city-proper populations (97 city-proper, 0 metropolitan agglomerations) anchored to stone-core hectares, earthwork perimeters, compound counts or contemporary enumerations [@WynneJones2018TheMultiple; @Lyne1905ZanzibarContemporary]. Tables 1 to 9 report linearly interpolated headcounts at five benchmarks (1500AD, 1700AD, 1800AD, 1850AD, 1880AD) alongside each settlement's peak population and date, marking spans outside observed occupation with a hyphen (-).

# Testing and Validation

Across all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements, ordinary least-squares rank-size regression yields $q = 0,73$ ($R^2 = 0,99$) across the upper 48 sites and $q = 0,98$ ($R^2 = 0,88$) across the full sample (Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank}). Chronological checks confirm clean continuity across Portuguese, Omani-Zanzibari and early colonial records without duplicate place-name aliases [@Baumanova2022WhatsName; @Parliament1898CorrespondenceRespecting].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 97 individually assessed settlements (top-48 OLS q = 0,73, R² = 0,99) and sub-regional densities in 1880AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## Omani-Zanzibar Sultanate and Swahili Coast

Table \ref{tab:sub-swahili} documents `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["zanzibar_swahili_omani_coast"]]), 0L)` settlements along the Swahili littoral and Usambara-Kilimanjaro hinterland, led by Zanzibar (65k), Mombasa (30k), Bagamoyo (18,5k), Pate (16,8k), Lamu (15,2k), Kilwa Kivinje (15k) and Siyu (11,2k) [@Allen1981SwahiliCulture; @Kusimba1999SwahiliStates].

```{r tab-swahili, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["zanzibar_swahili_omani_coast"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Omani-Zanzibar Sultanate and Swahili Coast sub-region (1500AD to 1885AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-swahili")
)
```

```{r tab-bemba, results='asis'}
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["bemba_lozi_zambezi_plateau"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Bemba, Lozi-Barotseland and Kazembe sub-region (1500AD to 1885AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-bemba")
)
```

## Portuguese Zambezi Prazos, Sofala and Gaza

Table \ref{tab:sub-mozambique} compiles `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["portuguese_mozambique_gaza"]]), 0L)` lower Zambezi, Sofala, Zimbabwe plateau and Gaza sites led by Vila de Mandlakazi (14,5k), Massangano-Zambezi (11,24k), Sofala (10k), Quelimane (9,2k) and Inhambane (7,5k) [@Pugliesi1977ResenhaLivro; @Newitt1995Mozambique].

```{r tab-mozambique, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["portuguese_mozambique_gaza"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Portuguese Zambezi Prazos, Sofala and Gaza sub-region (1500AD to 1885AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-mozambique")
)
```

# Limitations

Three constraints govern this gazetteer. First, 13 of the 97 entries carry single-date observations, so interpolated benchmark columns outside their observed year show a hyphen. Second, recovery favours coastal stone towns, Portuguese *feiras* and nineteenth-century caravan depots over dispersed rural villages [@HortonMiddleton2000Swahili; @Alders2023OpenAccess]. Third, summed gazetteer figures track nucleated settlements rather than full regional populations presented in the companion literature review.

# Conclusion

Together, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements trace the shift from sixteenth-century Swahili ports and Great Lakes earthwork complexes to nineteenth-century Omani plantation towns, caravan entrepôts and Zambezi *prazo* strongholds across 13 countries between 1500AD and 1885AD.

# Appendix

## Sub-Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} sums site counts and combined interpolated settlement populations across all nine sub-regions from 1500AD to 1880AD.

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- zone_entries[[sid]]
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0(sub_by_id[[sid]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1500AD` = sums[["1500"]],
    `1700AD` = sums[["1700"]],
    `1770AD` = sums[["1770"]],
    `1800AD` = sums[["1800"]],
    `1850AD` = sums[["1850"]],
    `1880AD` = sums[["1880"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0("All Subregions (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L), ")"),
  `1500AD` = tot_sums[["1500"]],
  `1700AD` = tot_sums[["1700"]],
  `1770AD` = tot_sums[["1770"]],
  `1800AD` = tot_sums[["1800"]],
  `1850AD` = tot_sums[["1850"]],
  `1880AD` = tot_sums[["1880"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated populations across nine sub-regions from 1500AD to 1880AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```
